answer: Cross-Epoch Trajectory Matching. Each identity's task history is embedded into a low-dimensional behavioral atlas; the system checks whether successive epochs trace a continuous path. A sybil cluster splits one real trajectory into many, so each copy shows an abnormally shallow path — a nadir in trajectory depth relative to peers. Enforcement compares path smoothness across a rolling window and weights influence by that continuity. An attacker must therefore run each duplicate through a full-length, plausible task river spanning many epochs before it gains weight,
